'''Thomas Clark Welsh''' (born February 3, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. As a senior in 2017–18, he earned second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]].

Welsh was a [[McDonald's All-American]] in high school. After leading UCLA in [[block (basketball)|blocks]] as a freshman [[Substitution (sport)|reserve]], he was a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] that won the gold medal at the [[FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] in 2015.  He [[starting lineup|started]] for the Bruins as a sophomore and junior, leading the team in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] while also continuing to be their top shot blocker.

==College career==
===Freshman===
In November 2013, Welsh committed to play at UCLA over fellow Pac-12 schools [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Kartje|first=Ryan|title=Four-star Welsh becomes third big man in 2014 class|date=November 20, 2013|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/welsh-537934-class-ucla.html|archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6Zu3aRVn0?url=http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/welsh-537934-class-ucla.html|archivedate=July 9, 2015|deadurl=no|df=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Dauster|first=Rob|title=UCLA picks up a commitment from top 60 big man Thomas Welsh|date=November 20, 2013|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/11/20/ucla-picks-up-a-commitment-from-top-60-big-man-thomas-welsh/|archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6Zu3iB8J5?url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/11/20/ucla-picks-up-a-commitment-from-top-60-big-man-thomas-welsh/|archivedate=July 9, 2015|deadurl=no|df=}}</ref> As a freshman with the Bruins in [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2014–15]], he spent most of the season as a backup to junior [[Tony Parker (basketball, born 1993)|Tony Parker]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Versatility could allow UCLA to highlight big men|date=November 3, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20151103/versatility-could-allow-ucla-to-highlight-big-men|archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6cy2W4V46?url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20151103/versatility-could-allow-ucla-to-highlight-big-men|archivedate=November 11, 2015|deadurl=no|df=}}</ref> Welsh played in all 36 games, starting in three, and averaged 3.8 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 3.8 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. He led the team in [[block (basketball)|blocks]], averaging 1.1 per game as a reserve.<ref name=kaufman_06172015>{{cite news|last=Kaufman|first=Joey|title=UCLA basketball: Thomas Welsh makes U19 USA Basketball team|date=June 17, 2015|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/basketball-667093-welsh-team.html|archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6Zu4058Ou?url=http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/basketball-667093-welsh-team.html|archivedate=July 9, 2015|deadurl=no|df=}}</ref> He became the Bruins' first 7-foot player since [[Ryan Hollins]] in [[2005–06 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2005–06]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/11852215/68-things-get-ready-college-hoops-season|title=68 things to watch this season|last=Brown|first=C. L.|date=November 14, 2014|work=ESPN.com|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103005731/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/11852215/68-things-get-ready-college-hoops-season|archivedate=January 3, 2018|deadurl=no}}</ref> In the season opener against [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State]], Welsh scored 14 points in 13 minutes of play.<ref>{{cite news|last=Helfand|first=Zach|title=At 7 feet, UCLA's Thomas Welsh may be a factor against Chanticleers|date=November 15, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20141116-story.html|archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/6Zu5AC7gL?url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20141116-story.html|archivedate=July 9, 2015|deadurl=no|df=}}</ref> He had six rebounds and four blocked shots in 22 minutes in an upset victory over [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] in UCLA's opening game of the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2015 NCAA Tournament]]. ===Senior===
Over the summer, Welsh worked on his three-point shooting based on feedback from his NBA workout with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He was the Bruins' lone returning starter in [[2017–18 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2017-18]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=USC basketball is ranked higher than UCLA in Pac-12 preseason poll for the first time since 2003-04|date=October 16, 2017|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/nba/la-sp-ucla-usc-basketball-notes-20171016-story.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111033647/http://www.latimes.com/sports/nba/la-sp-ucla-usc-basketball-notes-20171016-story.html|archivedate=November 11, 2017|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=New worries raise new questions for UCLA basketball this season|date=November 9, 2017|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20171109-story.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111033201/http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20171109-story.html|archivedate=November 11, 2017|deadurl=no}}</ref> On December 9, 2017, he tied a career high with 22 points and added 10 rebounds in a 78–69 overtime loss to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Thi|title=UCLA squanders double-digit lead, loses in overtime to Michigan|date=December 9, 2017|work=Inside UCLA|url=http://www.insidesocal.com/ucla/2017/12/09/ucla-squanders-double-digit-lead-loses-overtime-michigan/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215110025/http://www.insidesocal.com/ucla/2017/12/09/ucla-squanders-double-digit-lead-loses-overtime-michigan/|archivedate=December 15, 2017|deadurl=no}}</ref> On January 4, 2018, Welsh required three stitches after being bloodied by a hit to his nose. He was forced him to wear a protective mask after halftime, which affected his shooting as UCLA lost 107–99 in double overtime.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA falls apart in double-overtime loss to Stanford 107-99|date=January 4, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-stanford-20180104-story.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210204716/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-stanford-20180104-story.html|archivedate=February 10, 2018|deadurl=no}}</ref> He continued wearing a mask the following game, but adjusted for 19 points, 14 rebounds, and a career-high four three-pointers in a 107–84 win over Cal.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA reaches season high in points in 107-84 victory over California|date=January 6, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-cal-20180106-story.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107033217/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-cal-20180106-story.html|archivedate=January 7, 2018|deadurl=no}}</ref> On February 15, he played his first game without a mask since January and logged a career-high 17 rebounds along with 15 points in a 75–68 victory over [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA beats Oregon State 75-68 despite struggles from the free-throw line|date=February 15, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-oregon-state-20180215-story.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180218031208/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-oregon-state-20180215-story.html|archivedate=February 18, 2018|deadurl=no}}</ref>
